title: Priyanka Chopra Is Worth ₹2,507 Crore. She Built It Without Bollywood.
excerpt: The Fortune India–Interbrand ranking puts her at No. 3 — above Ranveer Singh, Akshay Kumar, and Amitabh Bachchan. She is the only woman on a standalone cover, and she hasn't had a Hindi theatrical release since 2019.
body:
There's a photograph on the June 2026 cover of Fortune India that tells you everything you need to know about the state of Indian celebrity in this decade. Priyanka Chopra Jonas stands alone — not alongside Shah Rukh Khan, not beside Virat Kohli — on her own standalone cover of the magazine's inaugural Most Valuable Celebrities issue. She is the only woman in the top three. She is the only woman with a standalone cover. And her last Hindi theatrical release was The Sky Is Pink in October 2019.

Seven years without a Bollywood film. ₹2,507 crore in brand value. Let that sink in.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ttQaw7tPFBc

The Ranking That Changed the Conversation

The Fortune India–Interbrand Most Valuable Celebrities 2026 ranking is the first of its kind — a study that moves beyond box office collections and endorsement fees to measure something harder to quantify: engagement, trust, distinctiveness, and cultural weight. The kind of influence that survives between film releases. And by that metric, only two people in all of India outrank Priyanka Chopra Jonas: cricket's king Virat Kohli (₹3,542 crore) and Bollywood's eternal emperor Shah Rukh Khan (₹3,017 crore).

"The study evaluated celebrities on parameters such as engagement, distinctiveness, coherence, affinity and trust — moving beyond traditional measures such as endorsement earnings or box-office performance." — Fortune India

The full top ten reads like a who's who of Indian pop culture: Kohli, SRK, Chopra Jonas, MS Dhoni (₹2,141 crore), Ranveer Singh, Akshay Kumar, Amitabh Bachchan, Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, and Allu Arjun. Three cricketers cracked the top eight. Only two women made the top ten — Chopra Jonas at No. 3 and Bhatt at No. 9. The message is blunt: Indian celebrity still runs on cricket and male star power. The exception is Priyanka, who built a different machine entirely.

The Empire Beyond Film

Here's what makes her ranking truly extraordinary: she didn't earn it by dominating a single medium. While Kohli's brand is inseparable from the cricket pitch and SRK's from the 70mm screen, Chopra Jonas has spent the last half-decade constructing a diversified global brand that doesn't depend on any one industry.

She is the Global Ambassador for Bvlgari (since 2021) and Bentley Motors (since April 2026) — two of the most exclusive luxury houses on the planet, both choosing an Indian woman as their worldwide face. Her hair care brand Anomaly, launched in 2021, has quietly become the second-wealthiest celebrity beauty brand in the world, trailing only Rihanna's Fenty Beauty. She produces through Purple Pebble Pictures. She invests in tech startups. She has a Padma Shri and a National Film Award sitting in the trophy case.

For the Indian diaspora, she is, quite simply, the most visible Indian woman on the planet. And she did it by stepping away from the Bollywood machine — not in anger, but in ambition.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZbozuNmxcC/

The Return Nobody Saw Coming

Which is what makes her next move so delicious. After seven years away from Hindi cinema, Chopra Jonas is returning to Indian screens — and she's doing it in the most audacious way imaginable.

She is currently on set for S.S. Rajamouli's Varanasi, an action-adventure epic being filmed in IMAX. Her co-stars are Mahesh Babu — making his Hindi debut — and Prithviraj Sukumaran. Chopra Jonas plays Mandakini. The film is locked for a worldwide theatrical release on April 7, 2027.

This is not a safe comeback. This is not a quirky indie or a streaming experiment. This is a Rajamouli film — the man who made Baahubali and RRR, the director who single-handedly forced Western audiences to take Indian cinema seriously. Choosing Varanasi as her return vehicle is a flex of the highest order: she doesn't need to ease back in. She's coming back at maximum volume.

What This Means for the Diaspora

The Fortune India–Interbrand ranking arrives at a moment when Bollywood's theatrical business is in its most competitive phase in years — ₹1,400 crore at stake across nine major releases in June alone. Box office collections still dominate trade conversations. But the ranking tells a more nuanced story: the most durable celebrity value isn't built at the ticket window anymore. It's built in the spaces between films — in brand partnerships, in entrepreneurship, in cultural ubiquity that doesn't expire when a Friday release disappoints.

Kohli proved it with fitness and lifestyle brands. Dhoni proved it by staying relevant years after international retirement. And Priyanka Chopra Jonas proved it by becoming a ₹2,507-crore brand without releasing a single Hindi film in nearly a decade.

For NRI audiences who've watched her navigate Hollywood red carpets, launch beauty products from Los Angeles, and then quietly fly to Hyderabad to shoot a Rajamouli epic, the Fortune India ranking confirms what they already knew. She's playing a different game. And the rest of the industry is still figuring out the rules.
